implementation_notes: Rust's standard library already models the bound kinds: a..b, a..=b, a.., ..b, ..=b all implement RangeBounds, whose start_bound()/end_bound() return Bound::{Included, Excluded, Unbounded}, so the classic two-field class collapses into std types plus a helper that compares the bounds. Membership is provided (RangeBounds::contains, stable since 1.35, and NaN-aware: a NaN is never contained), but overlap is not - is_empty() and IntoBounds::intersect() are still nightly (range_bounds_is_empty, range_into_bounds) - so overlaps() is written as an ordering check or by intersecting the two (Bound, Bound) pairs. Prefer a..b for sequences and time so that adjacency is exact.
pitfalls: Naive overlap for half-open ranges must compare Excluded bounds with strict <, while ..= bounds need <=; writing one helper for both silently reports adjacent intervals as overlapping (or as disjoint).

RangeBounds is implemented for the built-in range types and for (Bound<T>, Bound<T>) tuples, but implementing it for your own interval type gives you nothing: intersection, overlap and span remain hand-written either way.
Nightly-only is_empty()/IntoBounds::intersect() read exactly like stable API in the docs; depending on them forces a nightly toolchain, and the incomparable-endpoint (NaN) rules are subtle.
A float range never contains NaN - contains() is total-order aware - which is correct but surprising for code ported from languages where NaN comparisons simply return false in a different pattern.

variants.name: rangemap RangeMap / RangeSet interval containers
variants.implementation_notes: When many intervals must be stored and queried, the rangemap crate supplies the container std lacks: RangeMap and RangeSet are keyed by half-open ranges, RangeInclusiveMap/RangeInclusiveSet by closed ones, and insertion replaces overlapping ranges while coalescing adjacent ranges that map to the same value; overlapping(), overlaps(), gaps() and get() answer the queries a loop over a Vec cannot do efficiently. The crate documents the half-open-vs-inclusive decision explicitly (continuum key types want 0.0..1.0, domains that must include their maximum want ..=) and requires a StepLite/successor function for inclusive maps.
pitfalls: Insertion replaces overlapping ranges and coalesces adjacent ones with equal values, so the original boundaries are not preserved; use a splitting container or a separate key when borders matter.
RangeInclusiveMap needs successor/predecessor functions for the key type (StepLite or StepFnsT) because adjacent closed ranges cannot be detected by endpoint equality alone.
Removing a sub-range splits the stored range, so iterators and cached keys are invalidated by mutation; and the container is not a value object - it does not model the single-interval decision.
